When something is ingrained, it means it has become so deeply fixed into a person's mind, character, or way of life — or into a culture or society — that it is very hard to change or get rid of.

Think of it this way: imagine pressing ink so hard into a piece of cloth that it doesn't just sit on the surface — it sinks deep into every fiber. Even if you wash it, it won't come out easily. That's exactly what "ingrained" captures. Something ingrained isn't sitting on the surface. It has gone deep inside, become a firm part of something, and resists being removed.

The word is used for things that live inside a person's mind or character, or inside a group/society. The most common things described as ingrained are:

  • Habits — "He had an ingrained habit of checking his phone first thing every morning, even on vacation."
  • Beliefs — "Her ingrained belief that hard work always pays off guided every decision she made."
  • Attitudes — "His ingrained attitude of distrust toward strangers made it difficult for him to make new friends."
  • Prejudices or biases — "The ingrained prejudice against outsiders had existed in that community for generations."
  • Values — "Honesty was so ingrained in her that she felt physically uncomfortable telling even a small lie."
  • Fear — "After years of being criticized, an ingrained fear of failure stopped him from even trying."
The Key Quality: Depth + Resistance to Change

Two things are always true when something is described as ingrained:

1. It went deep over time.
Ingrained things are almost never sudden. They develop slowly — through years of repetition, upbringing, culture, experience, or environment. A belief you formed last week is not ingrained. A belief you've held since childhood, reinforced thousands of times, absolutely can be.

2. It is hard to uproot.
Because something ingrained is so deeply embedded, simply wanting to change it is rarely enough. It takes serious, deliberate, sustained effort — and even then, it may linger.

This is the heart of the word: depth that resists removal.

It can be either, depending on context. The word itself is neutral — it just tells you how deeply fixed something is.

  • Negative: "His ingrained arrogance cost him every relationship he ever had."
  • Positive: "Her ingrained sense of fairness made her a beloved leader."
  • Neutral: "The ingrained customs of the village had been passed down for centuries."

So pay attention to the word it's describing — that will tell you whether it's a good or bad thing.

You will often see or hear "deeply ingrained" as a pair. This just adds extra emphasis to show how extremely fixed something is. It's a natural, very widely used intensifier.

"Racism, in many societies, is deeply ingrained and cannot be solved with a single law."

You can use "ingrained" alone and it already implies depth — but "deeply ingrained" makes it even stronger and more emphatic.

Less commonly, "ingrained" is also used literally for physical dirt or grime that has worked its way deep into a surface and is very difficult to clean.

"No matter how hard she scrubbed, the ingrained dirt in the old tile floor would not come out."

This physical image is actually the clearest way to feel the word — dirt that is not just sitting on top, but has been ground down deep into the material. This is exactly the same logic applied to the non-physical (mental, emotional, cultural) uses.
Synonyms That Help You Understand It Better

Knowing similar words can sharpen your understanding:

  • Deep-seated — fixed deep inside, especially feelings or beliefs
  • Deep-rooted — like a tree with roots so deep it cannot be pulled out
  • Entrenched — dug in so firmly it resists any attempt to move it
  • Hardwired — built in so fundamentally it feels like it's part of the structure itself

All of these share the same spirit: so fixed, for so long, that change is genuinely difficult.

If something is ingrained, it has been pressed so deeply into a person, culture, or material — usually over a long time — that it has become a firm, stubborn part of it, and is very difficult to change or remove.
